name: mta-p4-exfil-decoy
title: Malware traffic analysis, Part 4: exfil and the decoy

slides.title: 14 domains blocked. One marked "do not block".
slides.sub: Part 4: what the host sent, the decoy, and what went into the ticket. FormBook/XLoader in an exercise pcap from malware-traffic-analysis.net.

slides.title: Seven POSTs per visit, the same total every time
body: 909 + 3,225 + 2,305 + 69,101 + 69,181 + 69,165 + 69,201 = 283,087 bytes per visit. 14 domains, 16 visits (two domains twice): about 4.5 MB.
slides.caption: Content-Length, not the Length column. Why: my Dec 11 post.

slides.title: Inside each POST: one encoded value
body: The body is a single 2kn1= value. I couldn't decode it from the capture, so the write-up says likely exfiltration, not what was stolen.
slides.caption: Each domain visited once sent back only 14 to 19 KB.

slides.title: The 15th domain answered like a real website
body: www.independent[.]ie got the same C2 pattern but only one 217-byte POST. It replied 301 to HTTPS from Cloudflare: a real Irish news site, registered in 2001, used as a decoy.
slides.caption: FormBook/XLoader hides its real C2 server among decoy domains.

slides.title: C2 or decoy? For 14 domains I can't say.
bullets: 13 were registered 72 to 156 days before the incident. Whois gave no date for the 14th.
VirusTotal flagged 12 of the 14. ThreatFox listed none (checked 2026-10-31).
Without the malware's config, the real C2 can't be told apart from the decoys. All 14 stay "C2 or decoy (unconfirmed)".
www.taibeinan[.]cc, the exception from Part 3, answered like a real website instead of 404. Why it still stays unconfirmed: my Dec 23 post.

slides.title: What went into the ticket
bullets: Contain: isolate DESKTOP-5NLV63K, reset rvance's passwords (browser ones too), reimage the host.
Block: the 14 suspicious domains at proxy and DNS, and the non-CDN IPs at the firewall.
Do not block: www.independent[.]ie, the Cloudflare IPs or taibeinan's CDN IP. Many legitimate sites share them.
Hunt: the fake User-Agent and the URI pattern on every other host.

slides.title: Four things this case taught me
bullets: Measure intervals, don't estimate them. The alerts suggested one minute, the delta column showed 24 s.
Pivot on behavior. The alerts covered 6 of 15 domains.
Finish enrichment before you name a domain decoy or C2.

slides.title: Cheat sheet: exfil and decoys
bullets: POST sizes: `http.request.method == "POST" && ip.src == <host>`, plus an `http.content_length` column
How one server answers: `ip.addr == <ip> && http`, then Follow HTTP Stream
Proxy hunt for this sample: User-Agent `Windows NT 6.2; rv:39.0`, URI path `^/[a-z0-9]{4}/` with `2kn1=`
Shared CDN IP? Block the domain, not the IP.

slides.title: That's the whole case
body: Scope, user, behavior, exfil. The write-up has every filter, frame number and IOC.
